criteria.text: The participant is male or female and is 18 years of age or older

source.text: Males and females \>=18 years of age

criteria.text: The participant has histologically or cytologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) based on a biopsy performed within the last 90 days, or has a prior biopsy showing NSCLC if the current biopsy is deferred due to unacceptable safety risk

source.text: Histologically or cytologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), performed on a biopsy that occurred within the last 90 days. This biopsy can be deferred if the procedure is deemed to represent an unacceptable safety risk to the patient by the Principal Investigator and as long as the patient has a prior biopsy showing non-small cell lung cancer.

criteria.text: The participant has a documented activating EGFR mutation (Exon 19 deletion, T790M, or L858R) on tumor samples tested by a CLIA-approved test

source.text: Documented activating EGFR mutation (Exon 19 deletion, T790M, or L858R) on tumor samples by Clinical Laboratory Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)-approved test

criteria.text: If the participant was treated with osimertinib or another EGFR TKI, they received no more than 28 days of treatment and have no evidence of grade 2 or greater treatment-related adverse events

source.text: Patients treated with osimertinib or another EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) (including erlotinib, afatinib, gefitinib, \& rocelitinib) are eligible if they received no more than 28 days of treatment, and if there is no evidence of grade 2 or greater treatment adverse events possibly related to treatment with the EGFR TKI.

criteria.text: The participant has a PET-CT within the last 60 days showing radiographic stage I to IIIa lung cancer

source.text: Positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT) within the last 60 days showing radiographic stage I to IIIa lung cancer (mediastinal staging biopsy is allowed but not required)

criteria.text: The participant has a brain MRI (or CT if MRI is contraindicated) within the last 60 days showing no evidence of metastatic disease

source.text: Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) (or CT if contraindication to MRI) within the last 60 days showing no evidence of metastatic disease

criteria.text: The participant is documented as a candidate for surgical resection of their lung cancer by an American Board of Thoracic Surgery certified surgeon

source.text: Documentation that the patient is a candidate for surgical resection of their lung cancer by an American Board of Thoracic Surgery certified surgeon

criteria.text: The participant has a tumor size of 1 centimeter or greater in its longest diameter

source.text: The patient must have a tumor size \>=1 centimeter (cm) in its longest diameter.

criteria.text: The participant has an ECOG Performance Status of 0-1

source.text: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status (PS) of 0-1

criteria.text: The participant has no unresolved toxicities from prior therapy greater than CTCAE grade 1 at the time of starting study treatment, except for alopecia and grade 2 prior platinum therapy-related neuropathy

source.text: Any unresolved toxicities from prior therapy greater than Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grade 1 at the time of starting study treatment, with the exception of alopecia and grade 2 prior platinumtherapy-related neuropathy is allowed

criteria.text: The participant's AST and ALT levels are less than or equal to 2.5 times the upper limit of normal

source.text: Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) =\< 2.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN)

criteria.text: The participant's bilirubin level is less than or equal to 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, or if they have documented Gilbert's syndrome, their conjugated bilirubin is within the normal range

source.text: Bilirubin =\< 1.5 x ULN, (Patients with documented Gilbert's syndrome and conjugated bilirubin within the normal range may be allowed into the study; in this event, it will be documented that the patient was eligible based on conjugated bilirubin levels)

criteria.text: The participant's potassium and magnesium levels are within the normal range

source.text: Potassium and magnesium within normal range, patients may receive supplements to meet this requirement

criteria.text: The participant's leukocyte count is greater than 3,000/microliter

source.text: Leukocytes \> 3,000/microliter (mcL)

criteria.text: The participant's hemoglobin level is 9 g/dL or greater, and they have not received a blood transfusion in the 28 days prior to study entry

source.text: Hemoglobin \>= 9 g/dL, with no blood transfusions in the 28 days prior to study entry

criteria.text: The participant's absolute neutrophil count is greater than 1,500/mcL

source.text: Absolute neutrophil count \> 1,500/mcL

criteria.text: The participant's platelet count is greater than 100,000/mcL

source.text: Platelets \> 100,000/mcL

criteria.text: If the participant's serum creatinine is greater than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, their creatinine clearance must be greater than 50 mL/min

source.text: Creatinine Clearance (CrCl) \> 50 mL/min for patients with serum creatinine (SCr) \> 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN)

criteria.text: The participant has the ability to swallow oral medications

source.text: Ability to swallow oral medications

criteria.text: Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 3 days prior to the first dose of study treatment and agree to use highly effective contraception during the study and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib

source.text: Women of childbearing potential (WoCBP) must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 3 days prior to the first dose of study treatment and agree to use highly effective contraception, during the study and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib

criteria.text: Women of childbearing potential are defined as women between menarche and menopause who have not been permanently or surgically sterilized and are capable of procreation

source.text: Women of childbearing potential (WoCBP): women between menarche and menopause who have not been permanently or surgically sterilized and are capable of procreation

criteria.text: Women not of childbearing potential are defined as women who are permanently or surgically sterilized or postmenopausal

source.text: Women NOT of childbearing potential: women who are permanently or surgically sterilized or postmenopausal

criteria.text: Permanent sterilization is defined as hysterectomy and/or bilateral oophorectomy and/or bilateral salpingectomy, excluding bilateral tubal occlusion

source.text: Permanent sterilization includes hysterectomy and/or bilateral oophorectomy and/or bilateral salpingectomy but excludes bilateral tubal occlusion; tubal occlusion is considered a highly effective method of birth control but does not absolutely exclude possibility of pregnancy; (the term occlusion refers to both occluding and ligating techniques that do not physically remove the oviducts)

criteria.text: Women who have undergone tubal occlusion should be managed as if they are of childbearing potential

source.text: Women who have undergone tubal occlusion should be managed on trials as if they are of WoCBP (e.g. undergo pregnancy testing etc., as required by the study protocol)

criteria.text: Women are considered postmenopausal if they are amenorrhoeic for 12 months without an alternative medical cause

source.text: Women will be considered postmenopausal if they are amenorrhoeic for 12 months without an alternative medical cause; the following age-specific requirements apply:

criteria.text: Women under 50 years old are considered postmenopausal if they have been amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of exogenous hormonal treatments and have luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone levels in the postmenopausal range

source.text: Women under 50 years old will be considered postmenopausal if they have been amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of exogenous hormonal treatments and with luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone levels in the postmenopausal range

criteria.text: Women over 50 years of age are considered postmenopausal if they have been amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of all exogenous hormonal treatments

source.text: Women over 50 years of age will be considered postmenopausal if they have been amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of all exogenous hormonal treatments

criteria.text: Acceptable contraception methods are listed

source.text: Acceptable contraception methods are:

criteria.text: Total sexual abstinence for the total duration of the trial and the follow-up period is an acceptable contraception method

source.text: Total sexual abstinence (abstinence must be for the total duration of the trial and the follow-up period)

criteria.text: A vasectomized sexual partner plus male condom (with confirmation of azoospermia) is an acceptable contraception method

source.text: Vasectomized sexual partner plus male condom (with participant assurance that partner received post-vasectomy confirmation of azoospermia)

criteria.text: Tubal occlusion plus male condom is an acceptable contraception method

source.text: Tubal occlusion plus male condom

criteria.text: A copper-banded intra-uterine device plus male condom is an acceptable contraception method

source.text: Intra-uterine device - provided coils are copper-banded, plus male condom

criteria.text: A levonorgestrel intra-uterine system plus male condom is an acceptable contraception method

source.text: Intra-uterine system (IUS) levonorgestrel IUS (e.g., Mirena), plus male condom

criteria.text: Medroxyprogesterone injections plus male condom is an acceptable contraception method

source.text: Medroxyprogesterone injections (Depo-Provera) plus male condom

criteria.text: Etonogestrel implants plus male condom is an acceptable contraception method

source.text: Etonogestrel implants (e.g., Implanon, Norplan) plus male condom

criteria.text: Normal and low dose combined oral contraceptive pills plus male condom is an acceptable contraception method

source.text: Normal and low dose combined oral contraceptive pills, plus male condom

criteria.text: A norelgestromin / ethinylestradiol transdermal system plus male condom is an acceptable contraception method

source.text: Norelgestromin / ethinylestradiol transdermal system plus male condom

criteria.text: An intravaginal device plus male condom is an acceptable contraception method

source.text: Intravaginal device (e.g., ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel) plus male condom

criteria.text: Cerazette (desogestrel) plus male condom is an acceptable contraception method

source.text: Cerazette (desogestrel) plus male condom (Cerazette is currently the only highly efficacious progesterone based pill)

criteria.text: The following contraception methods are unacceptable: triphasic combined oral contraceptives, all progesterone only pills except Cerazette, all barrier methods if used alone, non-copper containing intra-uterine devices, fertility awareness methods, coitus interruptus

source.text: Unacceptable Contraception Methods The following methods are considered not to be highly effective and are therefore not acceptable contraceptive methods:

criteria.text: Triphasic combined oral contraceptives are an unacceptable contraception method

source.text: Triphasic combined oral contraceptives

criteria.text: All progesterone only pills except Cerazette are unacceptable contraception methods

source.text: All progesterone only pills except, Cerazette

criteria.text: All barrier methods, if intended to be used alone, are unacceptable contraception methods

source.text: All barrier methods, if intended to be used alone

criteria.text: Non-copper containing intra-uterine devices are unacceptable contraception methods

criteria.text: Fertility awareness methods are unacceptable contraception methods

source.text: Fertility awareness methods

criteria.text: Coitus interruptus is an unacceptable contraception method

source.text: Coitus interruptus

criteria.text: Men with a female partner of childbearing potential must have had a prior vasectomy or agree to use effective contraception as described in the full protocol for at least 14 days prior to the first dose, during the study, and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib

source.text: Men with a female partner of childbearing potential must have either had a prior vasectomy agree to use effective contraception as described in the full protocol for at least 14 days prior to administration of the first dose of study treatment, during the study, and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib

criteria.text: The participant has leptomeningeal carcinomatosis or other central nervous system (CNS) metastases

source.text: Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis or other central nervous system (CNS) metastases

source.text: Stage IIIB, or distant metastases (including malignant pleural effusion) identified on PET-CT scan or biopsy (PET abnormalities that are negative for malignancy on biopsy will be considered on a case by case basis

criteria.text: The participant has a past medical history of interstitial lung disease, drug-induced interstitial lung disease, radiation pneumonitis which required steroid treatment, or any evidence of clinically active interstitial lung disease

source.text: Past medical history of interstitial lung disease, drug-induced interstitial lung disease, radiation pneumonitis which required steroid treatment, or any evidence of clinically active interstitial lung disease

criteria.text: The participant is known to be serologically positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)

source.text: Patients who are known to be serologically positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)

criteria.text: The participant has an active second malignancy, or a history of malignancy that has not been completely treated, or for which chemotherapy was completed <= 12 months prior or bone marrow transplant <= 2 years prior

source.text: Active second malignancy, i.e. patient known to have potentially fatal cancer present for which he/she may be (but not necessarily) currently receiving treatment; patients with a history of malignancy that has been completely treated, with no evidence of that cancer currently, are permitted to enroll in the trial provided all chemotherapy for prior malignancy was completed \> 12 months prior and/or bone marrow transplant \> 2 years prior

criteria.text: The participant is currently receiving treatment with contraindicated QTc prolonging medications or potent CYP3A4 inducers that cannot be discontinued or switched prior to the first day of study treatment

source.text: Patients who are currently receiving treatment with contraindicated corrected QT interval (QTc) prolonging medications or potent CYP3A4 inducers, if that treatment cannot be either discontinued or switched to a different medication prior to first day of study treatment. All patients must try to avoid concomitant use of any medications, herbal supplements and/or ingestion of foods with known inducer effects

criteria.text: The participant has any of the following cardiac abnormalities or history: mean resting QTc > 470 msec, clinically important abnormalities in rhythm/conduction/morphology of resting ECG, factors that increase risk of QTc prolongation or arrhythmic events

source.text: Any of the following cardiac abnormalities or history:

criteria.text: The participant has a mean resting corrected QT interval (QTc) > 470 msec

source.text: Mean resting corrected QT interval (QTc) \> 470 msec, obtained from 3 electrocardiograms (ECGs), using the screening clinic ECG machine derived QTc value

criteria.text: The participant has any clinically important abnormalities in rhythm, conduction or morphology of resting ECG

source.text: Any clinically important abnormalities in rhythm, conduction or morphology of resting ECG e.g. complete left bundle branch block, third degree heart block and second degree heart block

criteria.text: The participant has any factors that increase the risk of QTc prolongation or risk of arrhythmic events

source.text: Any factors that increase the risk of QTc prolongation or risk of arrhythmic events such as heart failure, hypokalaemia, congenital long QT syndrome, family history of long QT syndrome or unexplained sudden death under 40 years of age in first degree relatives or any concomitant medication known to prolong the QT interval

criteria.text: The participant received treatment with prohibited medications (concurrent anticancer therapy including chemotherapy, radiation, hormonal treatment [except corticosteroids and megesterolacetate], or immunotherapy) within 14 days prior to treatment with osimertinib

source.text: Treatment with prohibited medications (concurrent anticancer therapy including chemotherapy, radiation, hormonal treatment \[except corticosteroids and megesterolacetate\], or immunotherapy) =\< 14 days prior to treatment with osimertinib

criteria.text: The participant has any evidence of severe or uncontrolled systemic diseases, including uncontrolled hypertension and active bleeding diatheses, or known active infection including chronic active hepatitis B, hepatitis C and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)

source.text: Any evidence of severe or uncontrolled systemic diseases, including uncontrolled hypertension and active bleeding diatheses, which in the investigator?s opinion makes it undesirable for the patient to participate in the trial or which would jeopardize compliance with the protocol, or known active infection including chronic active hepatitis B, hepatitis C and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV); screening for chronic conditions is not required; patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) with negative HBV viral load on appropriate antiviral therapy will be permitted, if able to continue appropriate antiviral therapy throughout treatment period

source.text: Class II to IV heart failure as defined by the New York Heart Association functional classification system
